concerns.text: T004 is marked [X] (complete) but the description admits the implementation is missing: 'Create a function... that computes SHA-256'. The Constitution Principle V (Versioning) and Principle I (Reproducibility) require this state management to be functional before any data ingestion (Phase 3) can legally occur. A task claiming completion without the actual code violates the constraint that foundational infrastructure must be complete.

T012a and T012b are marked [ ] (unimplemented) but claim to fetch data from NREL and Materials Project. The spec FR-001 mandates downloading this data. The task descriptions contain placeholder text 'No address associated with hostname' instead of valid API endpoints. This is a semantic weakening of FR-001; the task cannot satisfy the requirement to 'download' if the endpoint is invalid or missing.

T014b is marked [ ] (unimplemented). The spec FR-002 and US-1 Independent Test explicitly require computing 'weighted_formation_enthalpy' and 'first_ionization_energy'. Without this task, the deliverable (descriptors) falls short of the FR/SC it claims to satisfy, violating the constraint that tasks must not silently relax what the spec demands.

T029 states it 'MUST use Benjamini-Hochberg correction' but only describes reporting p-values. The spec FR-007 requires the system to *apply* the correction to control the family-wise error rate. A task that only reports results without implementing the correction logic (calculating adjusted p-values) is a semantic weakening of the requirement to 'apply' the correction.

T030 mandates failure if literature data is missing. The spec SC-003 requires measuring the 'generalizability gap' (external R² vs CV R²). If the external data is missing and the task fails, SC-003 becomes untestable. The task lacks a fallback verification step or a mechanism to measure the gap against a proxy if the primary source is unreachable, violating the constraint that acceptance criteria must survive into the task's verification step.

T020e implements a fallback ('log a warning and proceed') if a perovskite family is missing. The spec US-2 and Constitution Principle VII require stratification by family to ensure independent test sets. Allowing the pipeline to proceed with unbalanced folds when a family is missing violates the strict stratification requirement, weakening the validity of the cross-validation metrics required by SC-001.
